messages:
marco: heads up — seeing a weird NVMe thermal/IO pulse in ap-south1, a handful of nodes failing GPU attach
priya: noticed increased write amplification on ephemeral volumes after last night's firmware push
sam: which pool? any host ids?
marco: scratchpool-7, sample hosts gnode-apse1-128..133. quick tail from dmesg: 
marco: ```
[ 12345.678901] nvme0: ctrl: aborting command, status 0x1e
[ 12346.000123] nvme0: media_error LBA range 0x1f4-0x2bc
[ 12346.500234] nvme0: temperature above threshold: 74C
```
alice: smartctl on gnode-128 shows reallocated sector count bump and temp=74C
marco: smart output snippet: 
marco: ```
Reallocated_Sector_Ct 0x0033 100 100 0 Raw_Value=4
Temperature_Celsius 0x0022 34 70 0 Raw_Value=74
```
priya: 74C spikes align with repeated small trims and fsync churn from janitor after fw change
sam: we observed janitor scrub cadence jump ~3x starting at 23:12 UTC — correlated with the rollout window
priya: hypothesis: vendor FW altered trim/GC timing => more small writes => write amplification + thermal pulses
alice: customer impact: GPU attach failures up ~12% in ap-south1 over last 2h, affecting batch launches
marco: created alert and linked it to ops ticket NVME-THERM-PULSE
ops-bot: Alert: NVMe thermal pulse detected on ap-south1 cluster. Incident: INC-2026. https://internal/INC-2026 :rotating_light:
sam: short-term mitigation options?
priya: throttle janitor, widen scrub window, or rollback FW. Also we can ghost/pin heavy smallwrite workloads off affected hosts
alice: draining affected hosts reduces attach failures but increases pressure on other AZs
marco: starting drain of gnode-128..133 now — ETA ~10m to finish allocations
sam: can we temporarily disable aggressive trim flag in kernel module? risky but less disruptive than full rollback
priya: we can test kernel-level flag on a canary host first; need to monitor write amplification ratio and temp
alice: procurement note: drives nearing end-of-life behavior under this pattern — open a ticket with vendor for firmware rollback option and RMA policy
marco: vendor already pinged, asking for definitive change log about trim semantics
priya: cost impact if we shift workloads to other regions: rough estimate +$1.2k/day if sustained due to spot premium and egress
sam: immediate plan: 1) drain affected hosts 2) throttle janitor cadence (30m -> 60m) 3) canary kernel flag on 1 host 4) vendor escalation for rollback
marco: doing 1 & 2 now, will spin up canary after drain
alice: adding perf counters to the dashboard: nvme_temp, write_amp_ratio, attach_fail_rate, janitor_ops/s
priya: anyone see user-visible corruption? logs only so far
sam: no user reports yet, only kernel I/O errors and elevated reassign counts
marco: update: drained 6 hosts, attach failure rate down from 12% -> 1.3% in 18m
alice: canary kernel flag applied to gnode-129, watching metrics
priya: telemetry so far: temp spike amplitude smaller on canary, write_amp_ratio decreased ~40%
marco: vendor confirmed firmware change to trim timing in this release; they've paused rollout and are investigating mitigation options
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 updated: status=mitigated, responders=[marco, priya, alice, sam]
marco: follow-up: schedule postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC, include firmware diff, janitor cadence change log, and procurement action item
alice: will draft postmortem and link perf charts
sam: ack
priya: thanks all — closing real-time ops, keep the thread for the writeup
marco: :thumbsup:
